**Short answer:** For an RV that runs a roof A/C, the strongest pick in these results is the **ALLPOWERS R4000** paired with a large solar array. If you're running mostly lights, a fridge, and devices, the **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2** with two 200W panels is a lighter option.

| Power station | Capacity | Continuous / surge | Max solar input | Weight | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [ALLPOWERS R4000](https://dealectric.com/allpowers-r4000-3456wh) | 3,456 Wh | 3,600 W / 6,000 W | 2,000 W (3 inputs) | 45 kg (~99 lb) | Best solar ceiling; not hand-portable |
| [EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/) | 4,096 Wh | 4,000 W / 8,000 W | Not stated in these results | Heavy, two-person lift | Most headroom; expandable past 12 kWh |

| [BLUETTI AC200L](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/) | 2,048 Wh | 2,400 W / 3,600 W | 1,200 W | ~62 lb | Budget pick with a 30A RV port |

**ALLPOWERS R4000 deal:** The listed price is $1,499 (list $3,299). Code EXTRA12 takes $179.88 off orders over $1,200, and the page says that brings it to about $1,319.12. It expires November 15, 2026. The page says the store accepted the code in a cart test on October 23, but checkout is the final word. ## Solar pairing

- **R4000:** Reaching its 2,000 W solar input requires panels on all three XT60 inputs, since each input tops out at 650 W. [Source](https://dealectric.com/allpowers-r4000-3456wh)
- **Jackery 1000 v2:** Its 400 W ceiling means two SolarSaga 200W panels use the full input. Adding more panels won't speed charging. [Source](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/)
- **Budget combo:** Renogy's 200W Foldable Solar Suitcase is a common pairing in these guides. [Source](https://nomadsignal.co/blogs/news/jackery-vs-ecoflow-vs-bluetti-vanlife)

## RV-specific considerations

- **Roof A/C is the big load.** A 13,500 BTU unit draws about 1,500 W running and spikes past 3,000 W at startup. On a 4,096 Wh battery at 85% efficiency, that's roughly 2.3 hours of A/C. A station with 3,000 W+ output is needed just to start it. [Source](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)
- **Without A/C,** a 2 kWh-class unit with a 300–400 W panel array covers most RV needs for a weekend.
- **Check your campground's 30A outlet.** Units with a built-in 30A RV port, like the AC200L and Delta Pro, can recharge from a pedestal without adapters. [Source](https://outdoorpowerstations.com/articles/jackery-vs-ecoflow-vs-bluetti-brand-comparison)

## Caveats

- Specs in these sources come from different reviews and model generations, so verify them on each manufacturer's page before buying.
- I don't have verified store links for the EcoFlow, Jackery, or BLUETTI units here. The links above go to the reviews that cover them.
- If you mostly boondock, check whether the R4000's 45 kg weight fits your storage bay.
